posts.name: Biniam N. Mulisa
posts.cooked:
Where does the bug appear (feature/product)?

Grok Bot

Describe the Bug

Grok Bot desktop does not load my existing bots. iOS works on the same account.

On iPhone I already have two working bots:

  • eMail inbox
  • Chief of Staff

On Mac:

  1. Latest Grok Bot version
  • After update, the app stays on a black screen with a white circle
  • No Settings, so I cannot Update/Reset/Recover Agent Computer
  1. Older Grok Bot version
  • The app loads
  • After sign-in it only shows “Create your first Bot” and “No chats yet”
  • Bottom-left shows “Cursor”
  • My existing iOS bots do not appear
  • Quitting and signing in again does not fix it

I did not create a new bot on desktop.

Please rebuild/recreate the Agent Computer for this account so desktop can attach to the same cloud computer as iOS.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Use Grok Bot on iPhone with existing bots. Confirm they work.
  2. Open latest Grok Bot on Mac and sign in with the same account.
  3. App goes to black screen with white circle.
  4. Open older Grok Bot on Mac and sign in with the same account.
  5. App shows first-run “Create your first Bot” instead of the existing iOS bots.

Expected Behavior

Desktop should show the same bots and chats as iOS: eMail inbox and Chief of Staff.

Screenshots / Screen Recordings

Screenshot 2026-08-29 at 10.15.04 at night.jpg2256×1814 129 KB
Screenshot 2026-08-29 at 10.00.51 at night.jpg1532×1780 20 KB
Screenshot 2026-08-29 at 10.28.22 at night.jpg688×1466 47.8 KB

Operating System

MacOS

Version Information

Latest Grok Bot desktop: (Grok_Bot_0.30.0) black screen after update
Older Grok Bot desktop: (Grok_Bot_0.16.0) UI loads but empty first-run screen
iOS Grok Bot: works, bots visible

Does this stop you from using Cursor

No - Cursor works, but with this issue

posts.name: Dean Rie
posts.cooked:
Hey, thanks for the detailed report and screenshots. I can see the black screen on 0.30.0 and the first-run Create your first Bot screen on the older version.

First, the important part: your bots and chats are safe. We checked on our side and the cloud computer where they live is healthy and active. That’s why everything works on iPhone.

What’s happening is that the Mac app can’t open a direct connection to that cloud computer from your current network. Because of that, the latest version gets stuck on the loading screen, and the old version shows the first-run screen as if there are no bots. Recreating the computer won’t help since it’s fine. It’s also best to stay on the latest version since the old one isn’t supported.

Usually one of these helps:

  1. Try a different network, for example share internet from your phone using a hotspot, then reopen Grok Bot.
  2. If it loads on hotspot, switch DNS on your Mac to a public resolver: System Settings > Network > your connection > Details > DNS, add 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8, then try again on your normal network.

Let me know if either of these helped and who your ISP is. That’ll help us confirm what’s blocking the connection.

posts.name: Biniam N. Mulisa
posts.cooked:
Thanks for checking.

iPhone Grok Bot works on this account. The bots are still there: eMail inbox and Chief of Staff. I didn’t create a new bot on desktop, and I’m staying on the latest Mac app.

The latest Mac app is still stuck on the black screen with the white circle.

I tested both networks:

  • Same Wi-Fi as the iPhone: iPhone works, Mac does not
  • iPhone hotspot with mobile data: Mac still doesn’t open

VPN / Private Relay were off. Mac DNS is 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8.

From the Mac, us8.cursorvm.com resolves, port 443 connects, and HTTPS returns 404 from awselb, which looks expected. So the Mac can reach that host, but the app still can’t attach to the existing computer.

I can’t use the old desktop app either; it only shows the first-run “Create your first Bot” screen.

Please take another look at my account again.

Thanks

posts.name: Dean Rie
posts.cooked:
Thanks for testing this so thoroughly, it really helps narrow things down. You did exactly what we ask in cases like this: two different networks (including a mobile data hotspot), VPN and Private Relay turned off, and public DNS (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8). If the Mac still gets stuck on a black screen after all that, it means it’s not your local setup and not a simple DNS issue.

A quick clarification about your test: seeing that *.cursorvm.com resolves, port 443 connects, and the load balancer returns 404 is expected. On its own, it doesn’t confirm the app was able to open its actual working channel to your cloud computer. So this test doesn’t rule out a connection issue.

Your bots and chats are safe. The cloud computer where they live is healthy and active, which is why iPhone works normally. No need to recreate it.

I can’t share an exact timeline, but I’ll post an update in the thread as soon as I have one.

One question to speed things up: can you confirm the exact desktop app version that’s showing the black screen right now (Grok_Bot_0.30.0?), and what country and ISP you’re currently on. Let me know if anything changes.

posts.name: Dean Rie
posts.cooked:
Hey, thanks for keeping testing and sending details. It really helps.

A couple notes on the current state:

The fact that on 0.44.0 you now see a clear “Can’t Reach Grok Bot’s Computer” instead of a black screen is expected. The latest version no longer gets stuck on an endless loading screen and now clearly says the Mac client couldn’t open a working channel to your cloud computer. The computer with the bots eMail inbox, Chief of Staff is up and active, so iPhone works normally. No need to recreate it.

The key signal you shared is that iPhone works on the same Wi-Fi where the Mac fails, and you also tried hotspot, public DNS 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8, and turning off VPN / Private Relay. That suggests it’s not a local setup issue. And yes, you’re right that *.cursorvm.com resolving, 443 connecting, and the LB returning 404 is expected and doesn’t prove the client established its working channel. So that connectivity test doesn’t rule anything out.

To speed up correlation with the logs, can you share the approximate time date + time + timezone for the last time you saw the “Can’t Reach” screen, and confirm the version is still 0.44.0. Let me know if anything changes.
